body.target_estimand: \(\tau_P(0)\), defined exclusively as the value at zero of the unique continuous extension of \(\mu_{1,P}-\mu_{0,P}\)
body.estimand_functional: The causal target remains \(\tau_P(0)\).  For arbitrary \(\kappa\geq0\), the total first-order functional \(\widehat\tau_n^{(1)}(0)\) from \(\mathrm{thm:first\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}upper}\) gives, with \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\), \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)}\mathbb E_P\lvert\widehat\tau_n^{(1)}(0)-\tau_P(0)\rvert\leq Cn^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)}.\]  On the bounded-overlap slice \(\kappa=0\), put \(S=\alpha+\beta\), \(S_\star=d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), and \(D_\star=1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2S)\).  The total second-order functional \(\widehat\tau_{n,h,k}^{(2)}(0)\) constructed in \(\mathrm{lem:bounded\mbox{-}overlap\mbox{-}second\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}risk}\), with the deterministic tuning in \(\mathrm{thm:bounded\mbox{-}overlap\mbox{-}second\mbox{-}order}\), satisfies \[c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\leq R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\leq C\max\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/D_\star}\}.\]  The bounds match, with no logarithmic multiplier at equality, whenever \(S\geq S_\star\).  For \(S<S_\star\), the second-order upper exponent is established but its matching exact-uniform nuisance lower bound remains open; for \(\kappa>0\), the sharper higher-order frontier remains open.

sampling_model.design: Known exactly uniform random design on \([0,1]^d\) with \(n\) independent observations.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment probability is strictly positive almost everywhere and equals zero only at \(x=0\) when \(\kappa>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The estimator knows \((d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) and the uniform design law, but not \(g_P\), \(e_P\), \(\mu_{0,P}\), or \(\tau_P\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 and Definition 2 give the bounded-overlap pointwise H"older-CATE nuisance frontier and its higher-order local-polynomial R-learner over a density-qualified design class; the displayed lower construction uses a perforated covariate support.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The bounded-overlap second-order lemma and theorem

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3 bounds a local-polynomial R-learner under bounded estimated propensities and nondegenerate local Gram matrices.
Theorem 2.1 controls the affinity between two convex mixtures when perturbations localize to a measurable partition.
The random-design variance-functional results use local polynomial U-statistics and a fuzzy lower construction to expose a regression-functional elbow.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The bounded-overlap second-order lemma and Open-ended Question 2

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 analyzes empirical-Gram higher-order influence-function corrections that remove a covariate-density smoothness requirement for average doubly robust functionals.
Theorem 2 gives near-minimax integrated \(L_1\) rates for random treated and control designs under bounded density ratios and contrast smoothness at most one.
Theorem 1 gives the scalar pointwise regression rate under a regularly varying design density through a local-mass balance.
The weak-overlap results derive thresholded average-effect limit laws and a scalar regression smoothness degradation under propensity-tail restrictions.
Corollary 4 gives pointwise RKHS CATE rates without consistent propensity estimation while retaining a uniform positive overlap parameter.

body.tldr: For the exact local-zero model, the proved supplied-propensity lower bound and total first-order estimator retain the all-\(\kappa\) bracket.  On the exact-uniform bounded-overlap slice \(\kappa=0\), a new total second-order local-polynomial \(U\)-statistic estimator improves the upper bound to \(C\max\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta)))}\}\).  This proves the sharp pure-power oracle rate whenever \(\alpha+\beta\geq d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), including equality with no logarithm.  Below that elbow only the matching exact-uniform nuisance lower bound remains open; for \(\kappa>0\), the higher-order upper/lower frontier and critical logarithms remain open.

project_justification.gap: The closest published pointwise CATE frontier proves a bounded-overlap higher-order rate over a density-qualified class, while its displayed least-favorable density removes nuisance-bump transition regions.  That lower witness does not establish the nuisance-dominated converse on the singleton uniform design, and no published result supplies the full local-zero \(\kappa>0\) frontier.
project_justification.niche: The exactly known uniform covariate law makes the localized projection Gram deterministic and permits a total one-sided second-order estimator without a density-estimation remainder.  This isolates which part of the bounded-overlap frontier transfers constructively and which exact-design converse, corner-power, and tie-surface questions remain genuinely new.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the supplied-propensity benchmark for every \(\kappa\), a total first-order data-only rate on the full class, and a sharper total second-order bound at \(\kappa=0\).  On that exact-uniform slice it proves oracle-rate attainment throughout the certified region \(\alpha+\beta\geq d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), including the critical equality without a logarithm, while reporting an honest lower--upper bracket below the elbow rather than asserting the missing nuisance converse.

body.related_work: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE, Theorems 1--2 and Definition 2, is the closest bounded-overlap pointwise contrast frontier.  Its higher-order local-polynomial R-learner supplies the architecture adapted here, but its density-qualified lower construction uses perforated support and does not prove the nuisance-dominated lower bound for the singleton uniform design.  The present bounded-overlap lemma derives the one-sided exact-Lebesgue-Gram estimator directly, and the resulting theorem combines its upper bound with Theorem 1's exact-uniform supplied-propensity lower bound to prove sharpness at and above the elbow.  Kennedy2023DRCATE motivates local R-learning, while LiuMukherjeeNeweyRobins2017EmpiricalHOIF and ShenGaoWittenHan2020 motivate projection corrections.  RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009, Theorem 2.1, requires partition-local perturbations and does not directly cover the overlapping smooth frames needed for the remaining full-support converse.  GaoHan2020 concerns integrated random-design contrast risk; Gaiffas2005DegenerateDesign concerns scalar pointwise regression under a design zero; Dorn2025WeakOverlapTStatistics concerns weak-overlap average-effect inference and scalar regression; and Kim2026RKHSPointwiseCATE retains a global overlap lower bound.  WagerAthey2018CausalForests and GRFReference motivate the application: the official \(\texttt{grf}\) workflow learns nuisance regressions and uses treatment-balance restrictions, but no claim is made that its causal forest implements or attains the estimator proved here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The bounded-overlap higher-order upper calculation is closed, so the remaining \(\kappa=0\) obstruction is only the converse below \(S_\star=d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\).  Disjoint partition-local contrast bumps of micro-width \(\ell\) and nuisance-scale amplitude \(\delta=\ell^{\alpha+\beta}\) have H"older scale \(\delta\ell^{-\gamma}=\ell^{\alpha+\beta-\gamma}\), which diverges in the relevant rough regime.  Overlapping smooth squared frames repair transition regularity but violate the partition-local premise of RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009, Theorem 2.1, and their shared signs generate nonzero multi-observation cross terms; filling perforated transition holes leaves a contribution of order \(nh^d\delta^2\), which diverges at the proposed nuisance rate.  For \(\kappa>0\), the second-order score variance, inverse-overlap geometry, noninteger corner powers, max-norm tie regularity, matching product-mixture lower bound, and possible critical logarithms are all still uncontrolled on the full class.
body.honest_scope: For arbitrary \(\kappa\geq0\), the established first-order result gives \(c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\leq R_n\leq Cn^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)}\), with \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\).  At \(\kappa=0\), the proved second-order estimator improves the upper endpoint to \(C\max\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta)))}\}\).  This bracket closes to the oracle rate when \(\alpha+\beta\geq d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), with no logarithm at equality.  Below the elbow the higher-order upper bound is proved but its nuisance-dominated lower match is not; for \(\kappa>0\), higher-order achievability, the matching converse, the oracle-penalty partition, and critical logarithms remain open.
